prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” broker for every self-employed person — the right broker depends on your ZIP code, budget, health needs, whether you want ACA Marketplace coverage (with premium tax credits), HSA-compatible plans, short-term alternatives, or an HRA/QSEHRA/ICHRA set up for your business. That said, here’s a short, practical plan to find the best broker in Kansas City, MO — plus some reliable places to start.

What to consider when choosing a broker
- Are they independent (can compare multiple carriers) or captive to one company? Independent is usually better for comparison shopping.  
- Experience with self-employed clients and ACA Marketplace plans (important for premium tax-credit eligibility and enrollment rules).  
- Fees: many brokers are paid by carriers, but ask if they charge direct fees for advisory work.  
- Licensing: verify they’re licensed in Missouri (Missouri Dept. of Commerce & Insurance).  
- Reviews and references: Google/Yelp/BBB, plus referrals from other local freelancers or small-business groups.  
- Services: do they help with plan selection, subsidies, HSAs, filing appeals, and year-round support?

Places and resources to start
- Healthcare.gov Marketplace (or the Missouri/Kansas state/local navigator organizations) — you can get free in-person or phone assistance from certified navigators or brokers.  
- HealthSherpa — a reputable online broker that specializes in ACA Marketplace enrollment and subsidy estimation.  
- eHealth / GoHealth — national brokers that compare many carriers and can be useful if you prefer online or phone-based help.  
- Local options: search for “independent health insurance broker Kansas City MO” and check Google reviews, or contact local SCORE / Small Business Development Center / KC Chamber for recommendations. Also ask in local freelancer/business Facebook/Meetup groups.

Questions to ask any broker you contact
- Are you licensed to sell individual/family plans in Missouri?  
- Do you work with Marketplace plans and help with subsidy eligibility?  
- Do you handle renewals, plan changes, and claims issues year-round?  
- How are you compensated and do you charge any direct fees?  
- Can you show references from other self-employed clients?

If you want, I can:
- Narrow this to brokers or agencies near your ZIP code and list top-rated local brokers (I’ll need your ZIP or neighborhood).  
- Walk you through estimated plan costs and subsidy eligibility if you share age, household size, and estimated income.

Which would you prefer?
